arguments.old_string:
WASH-OUT: perturbations applied at 2400 that are worth ~5e-4 nats at 2800 are worth exactly 0
by 3250. The trajectory re-equilibrates, so schedule/weight-decay tweaks cannot move the
crossing. Only a change to the descent RATE across the whole run can. Exchange rate near the
crossing: 0.001 nats ~ 20 steps ~ 0.035 reward.
arguments.new_string:
WASH-OUT: perturbations applied at 2400 that are worth ~5e-4 nats at 2800 are worth exactly 0
by 3250. The trajectory re-equilibrates, so schedule/weight-decay tweaks cannot move the
crossing. Exchange rate near the crossing: 0.001 nats ~ 20 steps ~ 0.035 reward.

The wash-out also swallows WHOLE-RUN step-size changes, which is the strongest single result
here. A from-scratch seed-0 run at lr 0.030 with floor 0.05 (peak lr +20%, tail lr identical,
everything else the same) is worse by 0.0072 at 1000, 0.0125 at 1400, 0.0093 at 2000, 0.0055
at 2400 -- and only 0.0005 at 3175/3200. A 25x mid-run gap converges to noise by the crossing.
So the entire lr-magnitude/schedule-shape family is a dead axis: it cannot move graded_step in
either direction. Iteration 5 should not re-tune lr, floor, land, hold, wd or momentum. The
only untested lever left is the update DIRECTION -- the preconditioner geometry (Shampoo/SOAP
eigenbasis Adam, a better polar approximation, per-layer or per-shape scale ratios between the
3 bucket shapes) -- or the split of work between the 72 owned matrices and the frozen aux
groups (which cannot be changed, but which the owned update can be shaped against).

Track-3 (nanogpt-speedrun-style, 124M, 3500-step horizon, target val 3.28). Measured 2026-08-15
on the H100 host. Method that works: fork a checkpoint of the real trajectory (custom trainer
replicating runner/full_mode.py exactly, checkpointing model+aux AdamW+optimizer state+data
loader position) and run variant vs control from the same state. Run-to-run nondeterminism is
~1e-4 nats, so forks are near-exact paired controls; a full 3500-step seed costs ~70 min, a
500-step fork ~10 min.

Baseline = iteration-3 rule (Muon + NorMuon per-row rescale, wd 0.05 lr-scaled, mu 0.85->0.95,
eta hold 0.32 / land 0.80 / floor 0.06). Seed-0 curve: 2400:3.37417 2900:3.29805 3125:3.28103
3175:3.27798 3200:3.27646 3250:3.27398. Graded crossing lands at 3200 (reward 0.5).

Iteration 4 re-ran that rule (plus a wd tail halving) on seeds 0,1 and landed on 3200 again:
seed0/seed1 3175:3.27777/3.27859 3200:3.27626/3.27709, mean 3.276675 vs the n=2 threshold
3.277172. Seed 1 tracks seed 0 within +0.0006 from step 2500 on; a mid-run seed lead of 0.003
at step 1000 had washed out to -0.0005 by step 2000. To reach 3175 the mean has to improve by
0.0011 -- that is the size of the prize, and no schedule-shaped knob is worth it.

Deltas at 2900 from a fork at 2400 (positive = worse):
  averaged-iterate (EMA) presentation, beta .99      +0.011
  EMA + hold lr at 0.25 instead of annealing         +0.044
  floor 0.12 (2x tail lr)                            +0.0069
  land 0.72 (faster anneal)                          +0.0036
  wd 0.05 -> 0.025                                   -0.0005 (decays to 0.0000 by step 3250)
Deltas at 1800 from a fork at 1200 (control 1600:3.51395 1800:3.47754; fork noise ~0.001):
  cautious masking of the orthogonal update          +0.025
  RMS-matched per-shape scale (Moonlight 0.2*sqrt)   +0.0074
  full-matrix whitening replacing NorMuon            -0.0004 (a wash, +6% wall clock)
  per-row rescale exponent 0.5 instead of 1.0        +0.0007 (a wash; full strength is fine)
  momentum 0.98                                      +0.038 at 1300 (bad transient)

TRAP: any mid-trajectory change that lowers the EFFECTIVE step size (lower lr, less weight
decay) shows a large instant val-loss drop -- lr 0.025->0.020 at a fork at 1200 reads -0.025
at step 1400 -- and it is entirely transient. Never score a step-size change from a fork
unless the fork is carried to the crossing. Both tail-lr directions are already bracketed as
losses (floor 0.12 +0.0069, land 0.72 +0.0036), so the back-half lr magnitude is near optimal.

WASH-OUT: perturbations applied at 2400 that are worth ~5e-4 nats at 2800 are worth exactly 0
by 3250. The trajectory re-equilibrates, so schedule/weight-decay tweaks cannot move the
crossing. Only a change to the descent RATE across the whole run can. Exchange rate near the
crossing: 0.001 nats ~ 20 steps ~ 0.035 reward.

Also: the tail is drift-dominated, not noise-dominated (~1e-4 nats/step descent at 2900), which
is why iterate averaging -- the in-trajectory stand-in for the records' eval-time weight
blending -- loses: a 100-step average costs ~0.010 nats of lag and removes less noise than that.

See [[track3-harness-facts]].

Probe telemetry went to `TRACK3_TELEMETRY_DIR`; `/telemetry` holds only this run.

**This ties iteration 3; it does not beat 0.5000.** Reaching 3175 required the seed-mean to improve by 0.0011 nats, and nothing I measured delivered it. The wd-tail change I added is honestly worth ~0 at the crossing (documented in the submission docstring).

## Why the search came up empty, and what it establishes

Every knob in the learning-rate/schedule family is now bracketed as a loss or a wash, measured against paired forks of the real trajectory: floor 0.12 (+0.0069), land 0.72 (+0.0036), cautious masking (+0.025), RMS-matched scale (+0.0074), full-matrix whitening (−0.0004, a wash), per-row rescale exponent 0.5 (+0.0007, a wash), iterate averaging (+0.011).

With the graded run finished at 04:16 and ~2.5 h of GPU left — not enough for a second graded run, and restarting one would have truncated the chain — I used the window on the one experiment forks can't do: a from-scratch seed-0 run at peak lr 0.030 with floor 0.05 (tail lr held identical). It is worse by 0.0125 at step 1400, 0.0093 at 2000, 0.0055 at 2400 — **and 0.0005 at 3175/3200.** A 25× mid-run gap converges to noise by the crossing.

That generalizes the wash-out result from late perturbations to whole-run step-size changes, and it's the useful thing this attempt produced: the step-size axis cannot move `graded_step` in either direction, so the next attempt should not re-tune lr, floor, land, hold, wd, or momentum. The remaining lever is the update *direction* — preconditioner geometry (SOAP-style eigenbasis, a better polar approximation, relative scaling between the three matrix shapes) — not the schedule. Both memory files are updated with the numbers and the mid-horizon transient trap that made the lr-0.020 fork look like a 0.025-nat win when it was worth nothing.
